text: “Yes.” “What kind of people are those ladies—the Misses Green?” “I really don’t know.” “That’s strange—when you live so near and see them so often!” “Well, I suppose they are lively, good-tempered girls; but I imagine you must know them better than I do, yourself, for I never exchanged a word with either of them.” “Indeed? They don’t strike me as being particularly reserved.” “Very likely they are not so to people of their own class; but they consider themselves as moving in quite a different sphere from me!” He made no reply to this: but after a short pause, he said,—“I suppose it’s these things, Miss Grey, that make you think you could not live without a home?” “Not exactly. The fact is I am too socially disposed to be able to live contentedly without a friend; and as the only friends I have, or am likely to have, are at home, if it—or rather, if they were gone—I will not say I could not live—but I would rather not live in such a desolate world.” “But why do you say the only friends you are likely to have?
